answer: An AI-agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to maintain a private sequential proof-of-memory chain that must be advanced once per epoch with non-parallelizable compute, similar to a raven tracing a single vine across the frozen tundra. An attacker spawning N clones must pay N full chain updates, each costing minutes of exclusive CPU, while an honest agent pays only once; the cost scales linearly with sybil count and yields no extra reward share.
